'''Jeffrey Demarco Teague''' (born June 10, 1988) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player, who is the head coach for [[Pike High School]] in [[Indianapolis, Indiana]]. He played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for five teams between 2009 and 2021, including seven seasons with the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. Since retiring in 2021, he has worked as regional scout for the Hawks.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/jeff-teague-rejoins-hawks-scout|title=Jeff Teague Rejoins the Hawks as a Scout|website=Atlanta Hawks}}</ref> Teague played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]] before being selected 19th overall in the [[2009 NBA draft]] by the Hawks. He made an appearance as an [[NBA All-Star]] in [[2015 NBA All-Star Game|2015]] and won an [[NBA Finals|NBA championship]] in [[2021 NBA Finals|2021]] with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].

==Early life==
Teague attended [[Pike High School]] in [[Indianapolis]], Indiana where as a senior in 2006–07, he averaged 22 points and four assists per game.<ref name=wake_bio>{{Cite web |url=http://www.wakeforestsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/teague_jeff00.html |title=Jeff Teague Bio |access-date=February 3, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180521021542/http://www.wakeforestsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/teague_jeff00.html |archive-date=May 21, 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Teague was listed as the No. 9-point guard and the No. 57 player in the nation in 2007.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/52340 |title=Jeff Teague – Rivals |access-date=February 2, 2016 |archive-date=May 10, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170510141641/https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/52340 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Jeffteague.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Teague as a college player, 2009]]
Teague played college basketball for the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]]. As a freshman in 2007–08, Teague was second on the team in scoring, scoring 13.9 points per game, just behind fellow freshman [[James Johnson (basketball, born 1987)|James Johnson]]'s 14.6.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/stats/_/id/154/year/2008/wake-forest-demon-deacons Wake Forest Demon Deacons Stats – 2007–08]</ref> As a sophomore in 2008–09, Teague became the first Wake Forest All-American since [[Chris Paul]] in 2004–05, and the 13th in school history. He was selected as a finalist for the [[Bob Cousy Award]], the [[John Wooden Award]] and the [[Oscar Robertson Trophy]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.wakeforestsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/020609aab.html | title = Jeff Teague Named Cousy Award Finalist | work = wakeforestsports.com | date = February 6, 2009 | access-date = February 2, 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151118174838/http://www.wakeforestsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/020609aab.html | archive-date = November 18, 2015 | url-status = dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=3974909 | title = Hansbrough, Curry make final ballot | publisher = ESPN | date = March 1, 2009 | access-date = February 2, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.bdasports.com/bda-athletes-jeff-teague/ | title = Jeff Teague | work = bdasports.com | access-date = February 2, 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160220192221/http://www.bdasports.com/bda-athletes-jeff-teague/ | archive-date = February 20, 2016 | url-status = dead }}</ref> He led Wake Forest in scoring with 18.8 points per game, in passing with 3.5 assists per game, in steals with 1.9 per game, and in three-point percentage at 48.5%.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/stats/_/id/154/year/2009/wake-forest-demon-deacons|title=2021-22 Wake Forest Demon Deacons Stats|publisher=ESPN}}</ref> He scored his 1,000th point with the Demon Deacons and became the 45th player in the history of the school to join the club.<ref name="wake_bio"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/290110154|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220311112033/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/290110154|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 11, 2022|title=North Carolina vs. Wake Forest - Game Recap - January 11, 2009 - ESPN|publisher=ESPN}}</ref> He scored a career-high 34 points on January 11, 2009, in a 92–89 victory over [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://godeacs.com/news/2009/1/11/No_4_Deacons_Top_No_3_Tar_Heels_92_89.aspx|title=No.4 Deacons Top No.3 Tar Heels, 92–89|date=January 11, 2009|website=GoDeacs.com|publisher=[[Wake Forest Demon Deacons]]|access-date=July 26, 2021}}</ref> On April 8, 2009, Teague declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final two years of college eligibility.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2009/news/story?id=4053791|title=Wake sophomore Teague to test NBA waters|date=April 8, 2009|publisher=ESPN}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Atlanta Hawks (2009–2016)===

==== Early years (2009–2011) ====
Teague was selected with the 19th overall pick by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in the [[2009 NBA draft]]. On July 20, 2009, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Hawks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://accesswdun.com/article/2009/7/221926|title=Hawks sign top draft choice Jeff Teague|work=haccesswdun.com|date=July 20, 2009|access-date=February 2, 2016}}</ref> As a rookie in [[2009–10 Atlanta Hawks season|2009–10]], he averaged 3.2 points, 1.7 assists and 0.9 rebounds in 10.1 minutes (.396 FG%, .837 FT%), playing in 71 games (three starts) and ranking tenth among rookies in assists. He finished the regular season in style, setting then career highs in several categories with a 24-point, 15-assist, five-rebound effort against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] on April 14, hitting 11-of-19 from the field and playing all 48 minutes.<ref name=nba-bio>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/jeff_teague/bio/|title=Jeff Teague Stats, Video, Bio, Profile|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=February 2, 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160323115814/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/jeff_teague/bio/|archive-date=March 23, 2016}}</ref> He went on to play sparingly in the team's playoff run, a run that saw the Hawks lose to the [[Orlando Magic]] in the Conference semi-finals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/teaguje01/gamelog/2010/|title=Jeff Teague 2009–10 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=February 2, 2016}}</ref>

In 2010–11, the second-year guard averaged 5.2 points, 2.0 assists and 1.5 rebounds in 13.8 minutes (.438 FG%, .375 3FG%, .794 FT%). He scored in double-figures 12 times, including three 20-point efforts. He led the team in assists four times and scoring on three occasions.<ref name="nba-bio"/> On March 12, 2011, he tied his career high of 24 points in a 91–82 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref name=br>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/teaguje01/gamelog/2011/|title=Jeff Teague 2010–11 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=February 2, 2016}}</ref> During the Hawks' 2011 first-round playoff match-up with the Orlando Magic, Teague played under 10 minutes in just two games, as the Hawks won 4–2. He was moved into the starting spot for the team's second-round match-up with the [[Chicago Bulls]] following an injury to starter [[Kirk Hinrich]]. Teague started all six games against the Bulls, a series the Hawks lost 4–2. Teague averaged 14.8 points and 4.2 assists in 38.1 minutes in his six playoff starts, well above his regular season averages.<ref name="br"/>

==== Breakout seasons (2011–2014) ====
[[File:Jeff-Teague-Atlanta-Hawks.jpg|thumb|Teague with the Hawks in January 2012|150px]]
Teague in 2011–12, started all 66 games, averaging 12.6 points, 4.9 assists, 2.4 rebounds and 1.6 steals in 33.1 minutes (.476 FG%, .342 3FG%, .757 FT%). He ranked eighth in the NBA in steals (106), 10th in steals per game, 20th in steal-to-turnover ratio (0.79), 22nd in assists (321), 23rd in assists per game, and 40th in FG%.<ref name="nba-bio"/> He had ten 20-point efforts and three double-doubles during the regular season, in addition to four double-digit scoring games during the Hawks' 4–2 first-round playoff loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/teaguje01/gamelog/2012/|title=Jeff Teague 2011–12 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=February 2, 2016}}</ref>

In 2012–13, Teague recorded career highs of 14.6 points and 7.2 assists, along with 2.3 rebounds and 1.5 steals in 32.9 minutes (.451 FG%, .359 3FG%, .881 FT%), appearing in a team-high 80 games (78 starts). He recorded ten 20-point/10-assist games in 2012–13, the eighth-highest total in a single season in franchise history ([[Pete Maravich]] – 12 in [[1972–73 Atlanta Hawks season|1972–73]], [[Trae Young]] in 2019-2020 - 16, 2021-2022 - 20, 2022-2023 - 11, 2023-2024 - 15,2024-2025 - 22, and [[Eddie Johnson (basketball, born 1955)|Eddie Johnson]] – 11 in [[1984–85 Atlanta Hawks season|1984–85]]).<ref name="nba-bio"/> On January 16, 2013, he scored a career-high 28 points in a 109–95 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20130116/BKNATL/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Hawks 109, Nets 95|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=January 16, 2013|access-date=February 2, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170510121725/http://www.nba.com/games/20130116/BKNATL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=May 10, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> Teague later participated in the Taco Bell Skills Challenge during NBA All-Star Weekend.<ref name="nba-bio"/> The Hawks were once again knocked out in the first round of the playoffs, losing 4–2 to the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/teaguje01/gamelog/2013/|title=Jeff Teague 2012–13 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=February 2, 2016}}</ref>

On July 10, 2013, Teague was extended a four-year, $32 million offer sheet by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]; however, three days later, the Hawks matched the offer.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-match-offer-sheet-teague|title=HAWKS MATCH OFFER SHEET FOR TEAGUE|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=July 13, 2013|date=July 14, 2013}}</ref> On December 26, 2013, he scored a career-high 34 points in a 127–125 double overtime win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20131226/ATLCLE/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Hawks 127, Cavs 125 2OT|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=December 26, 2013|access-date=February 2, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160718065104/http://www.nba.com/games/20131226/ATLCLE/gameinfo.html|archive-date=July 18, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On March 18, 2014, he tied that mark with 34 points in a 118–113 overtime win over the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140318/TORATL/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Hawks 118, Raptors 113 (OT)|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=March 18, 2014|access-date=February 2, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170314213615/http://www.nba.com/games/20140318/TORATL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 14, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> On April 14, he was named Eastern Conference Player of the Week for games played Monday, April 7, through Sunday, April 13. He earned his first Player of the Week honor after averaging 20.3 points, 5.8 assists, 2.0 rebounds and 1.8 steals in 33.8 minutes per game (.509 FG%, .917 FT%) in four games, in a week that the Hawks went 3–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/jeff-teague-named-nba-eastern-conference-player-week|title=JEFF TEAGUE NAMED NBA EASTERN CONFERENCE PLAYER OF THE WEEK|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=April 14, 2014|access-date=February 2, 2016}}</ref> The Hawks finished the 2013–14 season as the eighth seed in the East, eventually losing in the first round of the playoffs to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in seven games. Teague scored in double-figures in all seven games, including three 20-point nights, and had one double-double. He scored a playoff career-high 29 points on May 1, and notched his first career postseason double-double with 22 points and playoff career-high 10 assists on April 24.<ref name="nba-bio"/>

==== First All-Star selection and final Atlanta years (2014–2016) ====
On January 29, 2015, Teague earned his first All-Star selection as a reserve for the Eastern Conference in the [[2015 NBA All-Star Game]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/horford-millsap-teague-eastern-conference-all-stars|title=Al Horford, Paul Millsap and Jeff Teague Named Eastern Conference All-Stars|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=January 29, 2015|access-date=February 4, 2015}}</ref> Teague went on to lead the Hawks to a first-place finish in the East. In the first round against the eighth-seeded [[Brooklyn Nets]], Teague averaged 14.2 points and 7.8 assists per game. In game 6, Teague tallied 13 assists without a single point, helping the Hawks close out the series with a dominating 114–87 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150501/ATLBKN/gameinfo.html|title=Hawks beat Nets 111–87 to wrap up series in Game 6|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=May 1, 2015|access-date=February 2, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160201204021/http://www.nba.com/games/20150501/ATLBKN/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 1, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> In the Conference semi-finals against the [[Washington Wizards]], Teague averaged 16.3 points and 7.0 assists per game. In game 4, Teague recorded 26 points and 8 assists, scoring 10 points in the fourth quarter and hitting a clutch three-pointer in the final minutes, sealing a 106–101 win over the Wizards and tying the series at 2–2. In game 6, he recorded 20 points and 7 assists, while assisting [[DeMarre Carroll]] on two consecutive possessions in the final minute, giving the Hawks a four-point lead. They went on to win 94–91 after a potential tying three-pointer by [[Paul Pierce]] was waved off, clinching the series 4–2. They eventually lost to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in the Eastern Conference Finals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/teaguje01/gamelog/2015/|title=Jeff Teague 2014–15 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=February 2, 2016}}</ref>

Early on in 2015–16, Teague began to compete for minutes with back-up point guard [[Dennis Schröder]] as his role started to diminish largely due to Schröder's improved play and Teague's drop off in production.<ref>{{cite web|last=Dunlap|first=Michael|url=http://hoopshabit.com/2016/01/21/atlanta-hawks-jeff-teague-has-regressed-to-ordinary/|title=Atlanta Hawks: Jeff Teague Has Regressed To Ordinary|work=HoopsHabbit.com|date=January 21, 2016|access-date=February 2, 2016}}</ref> Midway through the season, Teague began drawing interest from opposing teams, with the Hawks reportedly talking with other teams about potential trades involving Teague.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoopsrumors.com/jeff-teague |title=Jeff Teague Rumors |work=HoopsRumors.com |access-date=February 2, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160202081920/http://www.hoopsrumors.com/jeff-teague |archive-date=February 2, 2016 }}</ref> On February 1, 2016, Teague scored a season-high 32 points and hit a career-high five three-pointers in a 112–97 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160201/DALATL/gameinfo.html|title=Teague scores season-high 32, Hawks breeze past Mavs|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=February 1, 2016|access-date=February 2, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160202195348/http://www.nba.com/games/20160201/DALATL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 2, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> Teague helped the Hawks reach the Eastern Conference semi-finals, where they were swept by the Cleveland Cavaliers.

===Indiana Pacers (2016–2017)===
[[File:Kyrie Irving (32963168585).jpg|thumb|Teague (left) with the Pacers in February 2017, guarding [[Kyrie Irving]].]]
On July 7, 2016, Teague was traded to his hometown team, the [[Indiana Pacers]], in a three-team deal involving the Hawks and the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-acquire-teague-young-trades|title=Pacers Acquire Teague, Young in Trades|website=Indiana Pacers}}</ref> He made his debut for the Pacers in their season opener on October 26, 2016, recording 20 points and eight assists in a 130–121 overtime win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/400899379|title=Turner's opening act leads Pacers past Mavs, 130–121 in OT|publisher=ESPN|date=October 26, 2016|access-date=October 26, 2016}}</ref> On November 9, he scored a season-high 30 points in a 122–115 overtime win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/400899560|title=Indiana holds on in OT, beats Philadelphia 122–115|publisher=ESPN|date=November 9, 2016|access-date=November 10, 2016}}</ref> He tied that mark on November 20, recording 30 points, nine assists and six steals in a 115–111 overtime win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/400899645|title=Teague, Pacers outlast Westbrook, Thunder 115–111 in OT|publisher=ESPN|date=November 20, 2016|access-date=November 20, 2016}}</ref> On December 30, he recorded a career-high 17 assists in a 111–101 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/400899934|title=George brings back fun for Pacers in 111–101 win over Bulls|publisher=ESPN|date=December 30, 2016|access-date=December 30, 2016}}</ref> In [[2016–17 Indiana Pacers season|2016–17]], Teague became the first Pacers player to start 82 games since [[Mike Dunleavy Jr.]] in 2007–08.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/400900604|title=Pacers push way into playoffs with 104–86 win over Hawks|publisher=ESPN|date=April 12, 2017|access-date=April 13, 2017}}</ref>

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2017–2020)===
On July 10, 2017, Teague signed a three-year, $57 million contract with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-sign-all-star-guard-jeff-teague|title=TIMBERWOLVES SIGN ALL-STAR GUARD JEFF TEAGUE|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=July 10, 2017|access-date=July 10, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2017/06/30/jeff-teague-minnesota-timberwolves-contract-rumors-update-free-agency|title=Report: Jeff Teague agrees to deal with Wolves|work=Sports Illustrated|access-date=January 7, 2018|language=en}}</ref> On December 27, 2017, in a game against the [[Denver Nuggets]], Teague suffered a Grade 1 [[Medial collateral ligament|MCL]] sprain in his left knee and was subsequently ruled out for two-to-four weeks.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/21902578|title=Sources: Teague out 2–4 weeks with MCL sprain|publisher=ESPN|access-date=January 7, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/jeff-teague-injury-update|title=JEFF TEAGUE INJURY UPDATE|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=December 28, 2017|access-date=December 28, 2017}}</ref> He returned to action on January 10 against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] after missing seven games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/400975357|title=Butler scores 26 to lead Timberwolves past Thunder 104–88|publisher=ESPN|date=January 10, 2018|access-date=January 10, 2018}}</ref> Starting 70 games, Teague helped Minnesota clinch their first winning season and playoff berth since [[2003–04 Minnesota Timberwolves season|2004]].

Teague missed six games early in the 2018–19 season with a bruised left knee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401070876|title=Towns, Teague lead Wolves over Nets after LeVert injury|publisher=ESPN|date=November 12, 2018|access-date=November 12, 2018}}</ref> On December 5, he had a season-high 18 assists in a 121–104 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401071043|title=Towns has 35 points, Timberwolves beat Hornets 121–104|publisher=ESPN|date=December 5, 2018|access-date=December 5, 2018}}</ref> He missed nine games due to left ankle inflammation between mid-December and early January.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401071247|title=Towns, Teague help Wolves recover in 120–103 win over Magic|publisher=ESPN|date=January 4, 2019|access-date=January 5, 2019}}</ref> The left foot injury kept him out for a further eight games between late January and early February.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401071496|title=Untraded Davis scores 32, Pelicans beat Wolves, 122–117|publisher=ESPN|date=February 8, 2019|access-date=February 8, 2019}}</ref> On March 21, he was ruled out for the rest of the season after reaggravating a left foot injury, originally suffered in December.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-medical-updates|title=MINNESOTA TIMBERWOLVES MEDICAL UPDATES|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=March 21, 2019|access-date=March 21, 2019}}</ref> On April 11, it was reported that the surgery Teague underwent for his left ankle was a success.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/jeff-teague-medical-update|title=JEFF TEAGUE MEDICAL UPDATE|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=April 11, 2019|access-date=April 11, 2019}}</ref>

===Return to Atlanta (2020)===
On January 16, 2020, Teague, along with [[Treveon Graham]], was traded to the Atlanta Hawks in exchange for [[Allen Crabbe]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Hawks Acquire Jeff Teague And Treveon Graham From Minnesota In Exchange For Allen Crabbe |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/hawks-acquire-teague-graham-in-exchange-for-crabbe |publisher=National Basketball Association |access-date=January 16, 2020 |date=January 16, 2020}}</ref>

===Boston Celtics (2020–2021)===
On November 30, 2020, Teague signed with the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-jeff-teague-tristan-thompson|title=Celtics Sign Jeff Teague, Tristan Thompson|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=November 30, 2020|access-date=December 1, 2020}}</ref>

On March 25, 2021, Teague was traded to the [[Orlando Magic]] along with two future second-round draft picks in exchange for [[Evan Fournier]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Magic Acquire Two Future Second Round Draft Picks From Boston In Exchange for Evan Fournier|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-acquire-two-future-second-round-draft-picks-boston-celtics-evan-fournier-trade-20210325|access-date=2021-03-26|publisher=National Basketball Association|language=en}}</ref> but was waived two days later.<ref>{{cite web|author=Orlando Magic PR|title=The @OrlandoMagic have waived guard Jeff Teague...|url=https://twitter.com/Magic_PR/status/1375840778166136833|access-date=March 27, 2021|date=March 27, 2021|via=Twitter|language=en}}</ref>

===Milwaukee Bucks (2021)===
On April 1, 2021, Teague signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] reuniting with his coach from Atlanta, [[Mike Budenholzer]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-jeff-teague|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Jeff Teague|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=April 1, 2021|access-date=April 1, 2021}}</ref> Teague played in 21 regular season games for the Bucks averaging 6.6 points 2.8 assists and 1.5 rebounds in 15.9 minutes per game.<ref name="Jeff Teague Stats">{{Cite web|title=Jeff Teague Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/teaguje01.html|access-date=2022-02-11|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en}}</ref> On July 20, 2021, the Bucks defeated the [[Phoenix Suns]] in game 6 of the [[2021 NBA Finals]], giving Teague his first NBA championship.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401344140|title=Bucks' 50-year wait ends with title behind 50 from Giannis|date=July 20, 2021|publisher=ESPN|agency=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=July 26, 2021}}</ref> He played in all six of the NBA Finals games, averaging 1.5 points, 0.8 rebounds and 0.5 steals in 9.3 minutes per game as the Bucks' backup point guard to [[Jrue Holiday]].<ref name="Jeff Teague Stats"/>

== Executive career ==
On March 9, 2022, Teague was hired by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] as a regional scout, returning to the franchise that drafted him in 2009 and where he spent his first seven seasons of his career, as well a second stint later in his career.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jeff Teague Rejoins the Hawks as a Scout |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/jeff-teague-rejoins-hawks-scout |access-date=2022-03-09 |website=Atlanta Hawks |language=en}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
On April 27, 2023, it was announced Teague would be the new head coach of [[Pike High School]], the same school he graduated from.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Former NBA star Jeff Teague returns home to Pike as new boys basketball coach |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2023/04/27/nba-all-star-jeff-teague-back-as-pike-high-school-basketball-coach-indiana-pacers-atlanta-hawks/70108470007/ |access-date=2023-04-27 |website=Indy Star |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Teague is the son of Shawn and Carol Teague. His father, Shawn Teague, played college basketball at [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]] for a year and then three years at [[Boston University Terriers men's basketball|Boston University]], playing under [[Rick Pitino]].<ref name="wake_bio"/> Also while at Boston University, Shawn played with [[Drederick Irving]], the father of No. 1 [[2011 NBA draft|2011 draft]] pick [[Kyrie Irving]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/more-sports/2012/02/17/jeff-marquisteague|title=Teague family at heart of hoops' little-man revolution|last=Jenkins|first=Lee|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|quote=Shawn's backcourt mate at Boston University was a gunner named Drederick Irving, who tried out with the Celtics and played professionally in Australia, where he had a baby boy named Kyrie.|date=February 17, 2012|access-date=October 8, 2025}}</ref>

Teague has four siblings, including [[Marquis Teague|Marquis]], who played point guard for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]] before being drafted by the [[Chicago Bulls]] in 2012.<ref name="wake_bio"/>
